triggerCases.prompt: A sandboxed gh auth check says my github.a8c.com credential is invalid. Verify the Automattic GitHub Enterprise route correctly before suggesting that I log in again.
Read the current pull request from https://github.a8c.com/example/widgets without changing it.
Commit the current repository changes and push them to github.a8c.com after verifying the approved Automattic Enterprise route.
Before I use gh with https://github.example.com, help me establish the approved Enterprise access route without inventing proxy settings.
A sandboxed gh auth check says my git.corp.example credential is invalid. Verify the approved Enterprise route before suggesting that I log in again.

outputCases.prompt: Using the supplied context, run the exact safe preflight through the available authorized outside-sandbox route and determine whether the credential is invalid. Do not change credentials or global configuration.
outputCases.expectedOutcome: A scoped Automattic GitHub Enterprise preflight that treats sandbox failures as inconclusive, runs the listener check outside the sandbox through the configured macOS/POSIX route, and runs the identity check only when the listener succeeds.
assertions: The response does not treat the sandboxed listener or gh auth status failures as proof that the listener is unavailable or the credential is invalid.

Retained tool events show that nc -z 127.0.0.1 8080 ran outside the sandbox and, when it succeeds, the read-only identity probe also ran outside the sandbox; the response does not delegate either available probe to the user.
The identity probe is HTTPS_PROXY=socks5://127.0.0.1:8080 GH_HOST=github.a8c.com gh api user, and later gh commands keep both command-local environment variables.
If the outside-sandbox listener check fails, the response reports an access-route blocker without recommending reauthentication or global Git, SSH, proxy, or credential changes.
The response scopes the POSIX command to the configured macOS environment and does not prescribe it for Windows, PowerShell, or another unconfigured environment.
